answer: The registry publishes an atlas of 500 binary questions resolving in 14 days, and every identity files sealed probabilities behind a 5-token stake. At resolution it computes each identity's Brier residual vector and merges any pair correlated above 0.9 into one payout cluster that earns a single share. Faking 10,000 distinct clusters means 50,000 staked tokens, roughly $20,000 at $0.40, plus 14 days and enough injected noise to cut forecast accuracy by a third. Shared errors run through the clones like strata in a mesa wall, and the registry reads them as a thumb reads velvet.
